entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Erwin von Steinbach, a German master builder (Baumeister), was the principal architect responsible for the iconic west façade of the Strasbourg Cathedral from approximately 1277 until his death on January 17, 1318. Operating within the vibrant artistic and intellectual milieu of the late 13th-century Holy Roman Empire, von Steinbach's work at Strasbourg represents a pivotal moment in the development of High Gothic architecture and sculpture, pushing the boundaries of structural innovation and narrative integration. His contributions cemented Strasbourg Cathedral's status as a masterpiece, influencing subsequent generations of builders across Central Europe and establishing the city as a center of artistic excellence.

Taking over the master builder's role, Erwin von Steinbach oversaw the construction of the lower sections of the west façade, including its colossal rose window and the intricate sculptural programs adorning the portals and galleries. He is particularly credited with the design and execution of the façade's monumental structure, which masterfully combined engineering prowess with a profound understanding of theological iconography. While the precise attribution of every design element remains a subject of scholarly debate, his tenure saw the creation of the renowned 'Church and Synagogue' allegorical figures, which became exemplars of medieval sculptural art, demonstrating a sophisticated interplay of form, symbolism, and emotional expression.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Erwin von Steinbach's master builder role at Strasbourg Cathedral from 1277 to 1318 produced a major High Gothic monument whose west façade became a direct prototype for numerous subsequent cathedrals in the Holy Roman Empire, notably Ulm Minster.
